What the numbers say

For the session of Monday, October 26, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as neutral. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is sideways and realised volatility is in the calm band.

11 of 26 tickers (42%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 19 of 25 (76%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 16 rose and 10 fell; the median move was +0.36%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Technology had the strongest average move at +2.34% and Communication the weakest at −2.10%, a spread of 4.44 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 1.35 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

1 ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (GOOG), and 1 at or above 70 (SHEL). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-23), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 38% to 42%, and the regime reading changed from mixed to neutral.
